This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 27.03.2023 at about 4.00 p.m., the petitioner alongwith others, was riding a Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HS-0375 proceeding from Kambipura (KR Market)
towards Kanakapura Road, after completing business related work.
After crossing the Anchepalya Masjid road in the direction of Bangalore, the petitioner parked the said scooter on the extreme left side of the road, infront of Anchepalya Masjid.

At that moment, the driver of the canter bearing reg No. UP-15-ET-4533 driving in a rash and negligent manner at a high speed and without any signals or warning, suddenly came and dashed against to the scooter, thereby causing the accident.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to Rajarajeshwari Medical College and Hospital and underwent first aid, thereafter he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore, where he underwent inpatient treatment from 27.03.2023 to 30.03.2023 and surgery.
The petitioner claims to have incurred more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical charges, food, nourishment and conveyance and other incidental expenses.

3. At the time of accident, the petitioner was doing business and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained, he asserts that he is suffering from permanently disabled, resulting in a loss of earning capacity and future income.
accident occurred solely due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he prays that suitable compensation be awarded against Respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of offending vehicle .
4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through counsel and filed their respective written statements.

5. The Respondent No.1 - Insurance company has filed its written statement and denied all the averments of the petition inter alia contending that the accident did not occur due to the driver of Ayub Raza Khayum vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27203080/
2 offending vehicle but, rather, the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence of the rider of motor cycle i.e., petitioner himself.

It denied the nature of injuries, the petitioner's avocation, income, treatment expenses, and extent of disability.
It has contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The compensation claimed is excessive and exaggerated and therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. Respondent No.2 has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.1 and policy, FC, RC were valid as on the date of accident.
That the driver was holding valid DL and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding in his Honda Activa Scooter bearing No.KA- 01-HS-0375 on 27.03.2023 about 4.00 p.m, near Bengaluru-Mysuru main road, Anchepalya,
Kengeri, Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, Benglauru District, due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the canter bearing number UP-15-ET- 4533?
2. Whether compensation petitioner is entitled ?
3. What order ?

doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.16.

On the other hand,
the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

9. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 27.03.2023 at about 4.00 p.m., the petitioner alongwith others, was riding a Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HS-0375 proceeding from Kambipura (KR Market) towards Kanakapura Road, after completing business related work.

As a result of the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

11. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 6 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.

To support of his claim, Dr.Chetan.A, Orthopedic surgeon is examined as PW-2 and he has produced the documents at Ex.P.14 to 16.
12.
As per EX P.5 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained Right leg both bone fracture.
It is mentioned that the injury is grievous in nature.

13. The Respondent-insurance company has contended that the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the offending vehicle but, rather, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
During the course of cross- examination, it was suggested to PW1 that he had crossed the road negligently, despite the absence of a designated crossing.
It was further suggested that he suddenly stopped his motorcycle in the middle of the road without observing the approaching offending vehicle.
However, the PW1 categorically denied these suggestions.

It is pertinent to note that beyond making such suggestions during the cross- examination, the respondents have failed to produce any independent evidence to substantiate their claim that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
14. There is no material on record to disprove the evidence of the petitioner or to substantiate the contention raised by the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborated by the documentary evidence produced by him.
Nothing has been elicited in cross- examination to discredit or disprove the petitioner's case.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After due investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.P.6.
Charge sheet along with other documentary evidence, prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Based on the above documents it is clearly established that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained a fracture of both bone in the right leg.
It is mentioned that the injury is grievous in nature.
Following the accident the petitioner immediately taken to Rajarajeshwari Medical College and hospital for treatment.
Subsequently he shifted to Hosmat hospital, where he underwent inpatient treatment and surgery.

16. PW-2 Dr.Chetan.A, Orthopedic surgeon at Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, deposed that the Petitioner had sustained a fracture in both bone of the right leg and underwent an interlocked Ayub Raza Khayum vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27203080/
4 nailing procedure of the right tibia on 28.03.2023.

sentences.text: Further, PW-2 stated that the petitioner now complains of pain and has significant difficulty in walking, climbing stairs, squatting and to drive cab.
Upon clinical examination, he has assessed the total permanent disability of right lower limb at 39% and disability of the whole body impairment at 13%.
17. PW-2 in his cross-examination has stated that he has treated the petitioner.
He also stated that the fractures have united.

While PW2 has assessed the physical disability of the petitioner at 13% to the whole body, it is noted that no opinion was offered with regard to the functional disability, which refers to the practical impact of the physical impairment on the petitioner's ability to earn a livelihood.

Taking into account the nature and location of the injury, its effect on daily and vocational functioning, the age of the petitioner, and the nature of his avocation, this tribunal is of the opinion that the functional disability should assessed at 9% to the whole body for the purpose of determining future loss of earning capacity and compensation.
18. In the petition, the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 60 years.
As per Ex.P.13 Aadhar card the petitioner's the date of birth is recorded as 28.11.1963.

accordingly as on the date of accident, the petitioner was 60 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 9.
19.
The petitioner has claimed that he was working as Sales Executive at M/s. S. A. Associate and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- at the time of accident.
In support of this claim, he has produced Ex.P.11 a letter which issued by the S.A. Associates, stating that the petitioner was employed as a sales executive and was earning Rs.35,000/-p.m.
It is further stated that the petitioner has not been resumed to his job due to his inability to perform duties as before.

However, the said employer has not been examined as a witness, nor has any additional documentary evidence such as pay slips,
bank transfers or employment records has been produced to corroborate the contents of EX P11.

In the absence of such corroborative evidence and non examination of the alleged employer, the authenticity and evidentiary value of the letter remains unsubstantiated and thus cannot be fully relied upon to determine the income of the petitioner.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023,
notional income Rs.16,000/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.
20. Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

21 . Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 9% is reasonable and just.
22. The petitioner was 60 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 9.
The notional income taken as Rs.16,000 x 12 x 9 x 9/100= Rs.1,55,520/- towards loss of future income.

sentences.text: Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .35,000/- would be just and fair compensation under head of Pain and sufferings.
24. Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .25,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
25. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.9 amounting to Rs.27,381/-.
There is no evidence forthcoming to disbelieve the said medical bills.
On perusal of medical bills, it appears that the petitioner has spent Rs.27,381/- towards medical treatment.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded compensation of .27,381/- towards Medical Expenses.
26. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.7 -Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was admitted at Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, as an inpatient from 27.03.2023 to 30.03.2023 i.e., totally for a period of 4 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .10,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
27. Future Medical Expenses:

PW-2 has stated that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implant which would cost approximately Rs.75,000/- Considering the potential future surgery, this tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/-
towards under head of future medical expenses.
28. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery,
this tribunal considers the 3 months for rest is considered .
As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 3 = Rs.48,000/-. loss of earning during laid up period.

29. Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of future earnings  1,55,520/-
2. Pain and Sufferings  35,000/-
3. Loss of amenities  25,000/-
4.

Medical expenses  27,381/-
5. Conveyance, Food,  10,000/-

6 6. Future medical expenses  15,000/-
7. Loss of income during laid  48,000/-
 up period  Total
Liability:
Respondent No.2 being the owner and the Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending canter are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

31. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs. 3,15,901/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
